result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Comparison.to_dict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: Get the comparison results as a JSON-serializable dict. twitter-card: title: >- [Comparison.to_dict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: Get the comparison results as a JSON-serializable dict. title: >- [Comparison.to_dict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get the comparison results as a JSON-serializable dict. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the comparison results as a JSON-serializable dict. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/_compare.py#L2265-L2377){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Comparison.to_dict( samples=True, limit=10, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A comparison is a live object that refers to the tables it compared. `to_dict()` turns its results into plain data that can be stored or sent elsewhere: written to a log or a database table, attached to a CI run, checked in a test, or passed to a dashboard. Everything in the dictionary is a string, number, boolean, list, dict, or `None` (dates and other values in the samples are converted to strings), so it can be serialized as it is. For a JSON string, use [`to_json()`](`pointblank.Comparison.to_json`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [samples]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Should samples of differing rows be included? Set to `False` when the data might contain sensitive values (e.g., PII) and only counts and schema details may be stored. [limit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The maximum number of sample rows per status. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[str, Any]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A dictionary with the comparison settings (`"source_name"`, `"target_name"`, `"mode"`, `"keys"`, `"compared_columns"`, `"column_map"`, `"schema_mode"`, `"null_equal"`, and `"partitions"`), the row counts of both tables, the results (`"n"`, `"n_passed"`, `"n_failed"`, `"identical"`, `"status_counts"`, and `"column_mismatches"`), and the schema differences (`"schema_diff"`, from [`SchemaDiff.to_dict()`](`pointblank.SchemaDiff.to_dict`)). If `samples=True`, there's also a `"samples"` entry, which maps each failing status that has rows to a list of row dictionaries, structured as in [`rows()`](`pointblank.Comparison.rows`). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's compare two months of an employee table and turn the result into a dictionary. ::: {#32fb92da .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl staff_jan = pl.DataFrame( {"emp_id": [101, 102, 103, 104], "salary": [52000, 61000, 58000, 47000]} ) staff_feb = pl.DataFrame( {"emp_id": [101, 102, 103, 105], "salary": [52000, 63500, 58000, 49000]} ) comparison = pb.compare( staff_jan, staff_feb, keys="emp_id", source_name="staff_jan", target_name="staff_feb" ) result = comparison.to_dict() result["status_counts"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'match': 2, 'changed': 1, 'missing': 1, 'extra': 1, 'dup_key': 0} ``` ::: ::: The samples hold the actual rows, keyed by status: ::: {#d13d6bd8 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} result["samples"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {'changed': [{'emp_id': 102, 'salary_source': 61000, 'salary_target': 63500}], 'missing': [{'emp_id': 104, 'salary': 47000}], 'extra': [{'emp_id': 105, 'salary': 49000}]} ``` ::: ::: Salaries are sensitive, so a record that's kept in a shared log might leave the samples out. With `samples=False`, only counts, settings, and schema details remain: ::: {#8c7e386e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} record = comparison.to_dict(samples=False) {k: record[k] for k in ["source_name", "target_name", "n_failed", "identical"]} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {'source_name': 'staff_jan', 'target_name': 'staff_feb', 'n_failed': 3, 'identical': False} ``` ::: ::: Leaving out the samples also means the tables aren't queried again, because the counts were collected when the comparison was made. To limit the samples instead of dropping them, set `limit=` to the number of rows to keep for each status.
